newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Friday on speculative buying with copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) failing to standing firm overnight above the key resistance figure of $2,400, traders said.

The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,620 yuan ($2,848) per tonne, rising 170 yuan. It opened at 23,650 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,660 and a low of 23,570 yuan per tonne.
May fell 10 yuan to 23,290, June rose 90 to 23,490, July 90 to 23,560, September 140 to 23,620, October 120 to 23,520.
Combined volume rose to 31,570 tonnes from 29,550 tonnes.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session.
Traders said speculative buying emerged later in the trading day on hopes that the LME will breach $2,400 per tonne.
"Speculative buying pushed prices up today with most investors counting on quick profits," one trader said.
Traders said any further movements in the Shanghai copper price would be dictated by the LME's Friday performance.
LME copper was little changed in early Friday trading, turning back from early attempts towards $2,400.
